proposed_widenings.name: ignore_difficult_terrain
proposed_widenings.justification: Difficult Terrain immunity is a categorical movement-economy effect — not representable as modify_speed (additive) or any existing speed atom. The TAXONOMY survey already flagged 'difficult_terrain' (2 hits) as genuinely new atom pressure.
proposed_widenings.evidence: Difficult Terrain doesn't cost you extra movement.

proposed_widenings.name: block_speed_reduction
proposed_widenings.justification: The ring prevents magic from reducing any of the wearer's Speeds. block_max_hp_reduction covers the analogous HP case but no parallel atom exists for speed. The source filter (magic-only) is also new — the existing speed atoms have no source-gating.
proposed_widenings.evidence: magic can neither reduce any of your Speeds

proposed_widenings.name: grant_condition_immunity (with sourceFilter: 'magic')
proposed_widenings.justification: grant_condition_immunity exists but is unconditional. The ring only blocks magic-sourced Paralyzed and Restrained; a physical grapple can still impose Restrained. Using the unconditional atom would overstate immunity. A sourceFilter field (e.g., 'magic') is needed.
proposed_widenings.evidence: magic can neither... cause you to have the Paralyzed or Restrained condition

notes: The unit fits magic_item / passive family structurally. All three gaps are at the atom/variant level, not the family level. The difficult_terrain atom is the most significant new addition — it was already flagged in the TAXONOMY survey. The speed-reduction blocker and source-filtered condition immunity are closely related: both are 'magic-source-gated protection' atoms that would likely share a common design pattern (a sourceFilter field on existing protection atoms, or a new block_magic_reduction umbrella). Could consider a unified 'magic cannot impose X' atom family rather than three separate atoms.
